topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the scope of the lecture on how innate immune components coordinate the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate immune recognition through PAMPs, DAMPs, and pattern recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the molecular sensors and signaling mechanisms used by the innate immune system to detect microbial products and cellular damage.

topics.label: Cellular activation, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic inflammatory responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how sentinel cell activation directs local leukocyte recruitment to tissues, drains antigens to lymph nodes, and can trigger systemic complications such as sepsis.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the immune system halts acute inflammation, repairs damaged tissue, and manages persistent insults through chronic inflammation and granulomas.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the subsequent lecture topic.
